extracted.intended_audience: IMLS staff, program evaluators, museum administrators, and grant program analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Metrics, sampling and selection criteria used in the RMC evaluation of the IMLS Museums for America (MFA) program, including representativeness checks, descriptive statistics for application/funding data, and criteria for selecting exemplary projects for qualitative study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representativeness (respondent vs. non-respondent comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare respondents and non-respondents on key characteristics (museum discipline, size, region, year of application, number of applications, awards) to assess whether the survey sample mirrors the selected pool. The report flags groups that are over- or under-represented (e.g., 'Art museums were slightly overrepresented...; history museums/sites were underrepresented...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-tabulations of counts and percents for respondents and non-respondents; report and interpret differences (examples in Sections C–F). Mark differences that reach statistical significance (see statistical significance threshold). Include explicit statements such as 'General/Specialized/Other types of museums were underrepresented in the survey respondent sample (16%) compared to non-respondents (29%).' and provide n and % for each cell.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag differences between respondents and non-respondents (or other comparisons) that meet the threshold '*Statistically Significant p ≤.05'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate tables/observations where p ≤ .05. The report uses this threshold to call out which representativeness differences are statistically significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response rate reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report survey response rates for each survey section (e.g., 'The response rate for this section of questions was 60%.' for Section C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sample size (n), response rate percentage, and note any exclusions (e.g., respondents excluded for no knowledge of project). Use response rate in assessing representativeness and potential nonresponse bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive statistics for application funding requests
rubrics_metrics.description: For groups of applicants report: Count, Total Request (sum), Total % (percent of overall requested funding), Mean request amount, Median request amount, Minimum (Total Request), Maximum (Total Request). (Exhibit B-1: 'The table ... presents the number of applicant museums, the sum amount of the requested funding to the MFA program, the percent of requested funding, the mean request amount, the median request amount, and the range of the requested amount for each museum discipline group.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all listed statistics for each disaggregation (discipline, size, region, state) and the overall totals. Report ranges (min–max) and interpretable central tendency measures (mean and median), especially because request distributions may be skewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaggregation by grouping variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Present application and award statistics disaggregated by museum discipline, museum size, region, and state (e.g., 'MFA Application Funding Requests by Museum Discipline', 'by Museum Size', 'by Region', 'by State').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show counts and the same descriptive statistics (sum, percent, mean, median, min, max) within each group to identify patterns across strata (for example: 'Almost half (49%) of the total requested funding was made by large museums').

rubrics_metrics.name: Award and project characteristic categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Report award-level categorical breakdowns such as award amount bands (<$50,000; $50,000–99,000; $100,000 or more), number of project years (Less than 2; 2 Years; Over 2 Years), extension status (None; 1 or more), and primary area where resources were spent (Programming; Exhibits; Digitization; Collections; Technology and online resources; Organizational development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide n and % for each category and note distributional patterns (e.g., percent in each award band, percent with extensions). Use these categories consistently across sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum background / demographics metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and report museum-level background variables: Governance (Non-profit vs All Other), Museum opening year categories (Before 1900; 1900–1925; 1926–1950; 1951–1975; 1976–1999; 2000 or after), Number of people holding leadership role since 2004 (1; 2; 3+), Number of paid employees (10 or less; 11–40; over 40), Average number of unpaid staff (Less than 30; 30–109; 110 or more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts and percents for each demographic category; use these to analyze representativeness and to describe respondent characteristics (Exhibits A-11 through A-22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant experience and application history metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure applicant prior behavior with items such as 'Number of IMLS Applications in the Past Year', 'Number of Other IMLS Applications Ever Submitted', 'Of Those Applying Number of Other IMLS Awards Received', and whether the museum 'applied for any federal agency grants other than to IMLS'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts and percents (None, 1, 2 or more) and use these metrics to examine relationships between experience and response propensity or success (the report notes, for example, that 'museums with extensive experience ... were over-represented').

rubrics_metrics.name: Project continuation status
rubrics_metrics.description: Report whether the project led to a continuation application or was itself a continuation ('When asked about the continuation status of their project, 60% reported that the project did not lead to a continuation application, 33% said it did lead to another application to continue the project, and 7% said the project was a continuation of a prior award.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide n and % and consider continuation status when interpreting project impact and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived grant size relative to other grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask respondents to compare the MFA grant to other grants they received (options such as 'about the same', 'larger', 'smaller') and report distribution (e.g., '46% ... about the same, 42% said it was larger, and 13% said it was smaller').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report by museum size where relevant (the report notes differences by small/medium/large museums). Use to contextualize award sufficiency and perceived impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization for exemplar selection (urban/rural x operating budget)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize completed projects into four groups for exemplar selection: urban location & small operating budget (<$1.5 million), rural location & small operating budget, urban location & large operating budget (≥$1.5 million), and rural location & large operating budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories to ensure balanced representation of project types when selecting exemplary projects for qualitative study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplary project nomination and selection criteria (qualitative sample)
rubrics_metrics.description: When MFA staff recommended projects for best-practice profiles, they were asked to consider: 'The project involved a wide range of project activities; There were still knowledgeable staff available to report on the project; Project activities have been somewhat sustained beyond the grant period; Known challenges would be beneficial to share with the museum field; Community members were impacted by the project; and Organizational changes occurred due to the project.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these substantive criteria to nominate and vet candidate projects; document nomination rationale and then further analyze the pool by region, discipline, and grant size before final selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative data collection procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Document qualitative methods: collect final performance reports, conduct one- to one-and-a-half-hour telephone interviews, and for selected cases perform two-day site visits including video interviews and on-site observation. (The report: 'RMC staff conducted one- to one-and-a-half hour telephone interviews...' and site visits of two days for six projects.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record who was interviewed, interview duration, and any site-visit activities. Provide a list of selected projects with indicators for Interview (I) and Site Visit (SV). Use qualitative data to 'deepen the understanding of the quantitative data.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting sample sizes and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always state sample sizes (n) for each section and note exclusions (e.g., Section D sample size was 537 after excluding 12 respondents 'having no knowledge of the project').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transparent accounting of initial pool, selected sample, respondents, non-respondents, and any exclusions so that percentages and representativeness claims are reproducible.
